column7: 2026-11-04: parseBytes: decimal units (kB/MB/GB...) deliberately unsupported (throw SyntaxError) until the user hears back from the storage team on how to read them. Signs/exponents/thousands separators also rejected.

2026-11-04: Storage team answer: on this branch, non-i units are powers of 1024 (users paste from Windows Explorer): '1 KB' or '1 kB' = 1024, '1 MB' = 1048576. To be added in a later session; not in the first parseBytes commit.

2026-11-04: billing-svc pins this branch: parseBytes supports plain numbers and binary units (B, KiB..YiB) only; decimal kB/MB/GB deliberately unsupported for now (billing asked). Branch is at the same commit as storage-app (da12924); storage team's 1024-based reading of KB/MB is a storage-app decision, not adopted here.

2026-11-04: billing-svc: when decimal units are added, they are strict SI: 1 kB = 1000, 1 MB = 1,000,000 bytes, matching prettyBytes' non-binary output. Reason: billing quotes in strict SI. Differs from storage-app, which reads KB/MB as 1024 powers.
2026-11-04: parseBytes now accepts kB/KB (both = 1024), MB..YB as powers of 1024, per storage team answer; other cases (kb, mB, Mb) still throw. Documented in readme.
